newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end lower in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end lower in Tokyo.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen futures contract settled down but off its lows in Tokyo on Wednesday after earlier slipping briefly to 98.78, its lowest since July 29, 1996.

Heavy sales of Japanese government bonds (JGBs) on an announcement that Standard and Poor's (S&P's) had assigned a Bpi rating to three Japanese life insurers pushed the December down. It settled at 98.79 after moving from 98.78 to 98.86.

Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co, Kyoei Life Insurance Co Ltd and Nippon Dantai Life Insurance Co Ltd all received the Bpi rating from S&P, raising concerns that these companies might sell JGBs, bond traders said.

Downward pressure from the JGB market appeared to have sparked some speculative tests of the downside for the December Euroyen contract, a city bank dealer said. "We may see consolidation near the 98.78-98.80 level," he added.
No immediate impact was seen from a news conference by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita as the market had closed.
Matsushita said that monetary policy is unchanged and aimed at strengthening economic recovery.

"The market is much more concerned about tomorrow's industrial production figures, particularly predictions for June," the city bank dealer said. Industrial production data is due out at 0430 GMT Thursday.
In the Interest Rate Swap (IRS) market, payment by some Japanese banks for short-term maturities was detected.
The two-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.46/1.50 percent against 1.38/1.42 percent on Tuesday and sparked some hedge sales of the December Euroyen contract, dealers said.

In the interbank market, key overnight call money was traded at around 0.53 against Tuesday's 0.52 percent, while around 100 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.60 percent, the same as Tuesday.

"Unless the BOJ starts performing accomodative operations, the overnight rate is likely to keep edging up, particularly in the face of month-end funds demand," one trader said. But he added that the central bank still may hold off performing such operations. The BOJ injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market this morning against a shortfall of 380 billion yen, less than expected by some in the market.
